Several LDL subclasses have been identiﬁed using gradient gel electrophoresis. Large, less dense LDL particles are commonly
found in premenopausal women and men at low risk for CHD, whereas the small, more dense particles have been associated
with a signiﬁcant increased risk for myocardial infarction. The distribution of these particles appears to have a signiﬁcant genetic
component modulated by age and environmental factors.
